sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Type checking and import shortcuts
sections.what: Tells the TypeScript checker which language features to allow, how strict to be, and that the @ symbol points to the project root. Visitors do not see this file directly.
sections.why: Likely reason: stricter checking catches errors early, and the @ shortcut keeps imports tidy.
sections.watch_out: Changing the paths setting breaks every import that uses @ until it is corrected.

summary: Settings for the TypeScript checker that tell it how strict to be, which browser features to allow, and how to find files with the @ shortcut.
purpose: Controls how the code is checked for mistakes and how imports are resolved.
why: Strict checking catches many errors before the site runs. The @ shortcut lets files import from the project root without long relative paths.
how: The editor and build read this file. The strict option checks types, and the paths option maps the @ symbol to the project root so imports such as components can be found.
inputs: All TypeScript and TSX files in the project.
outputs: Type errors or warnings, and resolved import paths. It does not produce output files because no emitting is allowed.
risks: Turning off strict mode would hide type problems. The include rules scan many files, which can slow checking slightly.
debug: If an import like components cannot be found, check the paths setting and the file location. If the editor shows type errors, compare with the build output.
